summary: Learn causal inference for policy and business decisions with hands-on methods, practical datasets, and decision-ready reporting.
lede: Causal inference for policy, programmes and business decisions helps you estimate what would have happened without an intervention, distinguish correlation from causation, and produce evidence that can withstand scrutiny. This course develops practical skills in counterfactual thinking, treatment-effect estimation, confounding control, evaluation design, and results interpretation. You will learn to frame causal questions, define treatment and control groups, choose suitable study designs, and test identification assumptions using realistic datasets and repeatable templates. You will then turn your analysis into evaluation memos, impact summaries, and decision briefs that connect actions to defensible conclusions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to evaluate interventions, defend attribution claims, and brief decision-makers with credible causal evidence in policy, programme, and business settings.
prerequisites: You should have working knowledge of basic statistics, including hypothesis testing, linear regression, probability, and confidence intervals. Familiarity with one statistical environment such as R, Stata, or Python is recommended, but coding is not required for conceptual participation; advanced estimation exercises will be demonstrated through guided workflows. Prior exposure to evaluation design, program monitoring, or business analytics will help you move faster, although the course is structured for intermediate learners who need practical causal inference for policy, programmes and business decisions capability. Advanced concepts such as identification strategy, target trial emulation, and sensitivity analysis are taught at the operational application level, not as production-grade engineering.
topics: Statistics & data analysis (SPSS, Stata, R, Python)
